summary: Korg's Pitchclip 2 instructions identify the clip, display and power button and describe adjusting the display angle. Follow the closing flap through its arc.
intro: A tuner can fit the outline on a drawing and still arrive with its display pressed against a closure flap. The difference is often the angle at which the head was packed. Agree a repeatable position with the brand, sketch it in section and size the saddle around the approved support points on the clip.
faq: How should a clip-on tuner sit inside a folded mailer?
Fix one packed display angle in the assembly drawing so the screen stays below the closing flap arc and does not press against the outer carton.
Should the insert grip the tuner clip jaws?
No. Support the rigid body housing rather than forcing the rubberized clip pads open during storage.
What is the minimum order quantity for custom tuner mailers?
MTT Packaging produces custom folding cartons and mailers from 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 minimum product value per order.
cta: Send a side view at the approved screen angle, a packed sample and the leaflet fold for a tuner saddle review. Include quantity and destination. Minimum 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 product value per order, excluding freight, samples and other fees.
sections: Trace the complete packed profile

Korg's Pitchclip 2 instructions identify the clip, display and power button and describe adjusting the display angle. For your model, obtain the intended shipping position from its supplier. Mark the highest display edge and the button location with the device resting on the proposed saddle. Leave the battery configuration and any transport documentation to the responsible product owner.
Follow the closing flap through its arc

A flap can sweep through the screen space even when it clears the display once closed. Fold a full-size board sample slowly around a dummy and watch the leading edge. Compare trimming that flap with shifting the tuner away from the fold. Keep enough engagement for the chosen closure, and check that the revised saddle still permits unloading by the clip body.
Agree what to inspect after handling

Open the loaded mailer on a level surface and note whether the head angle changed, the display contacted the board or the clip slid off its saddle. Have the device owner specify the appropriate functional check. Keep a photograph of the approved side view at the packing station; quoting a new board grade without controlling the pack position can leave the original interference unchanged.

Request separate prices for the presentation box, insert, sample and shipping outer.

title: Packing a Pick Assortment So the Player Can Identify Every Gauge
seoTitle: Packing a Pick Assortment So the Player Can Identify Every Gauge
summary: Dunlop's standard range includes several gauges and variety packs. Calculate height from full envelopes.
intro: A musician opening a sampler may want to compare two gauges and return each pick to its place. A tube full of loose picks gives the packer a fast fill but leaves the player sorting them on a table. Build the packaging brief around how the customer will identify and replace a single pick after opening.
faq: Why can multiplying pick thickness underestimate assortment box depth?
Sealed polybags, folded header cards, and air pockets add stack height beyond the sum of bare celluloid or nylon pick gauges.
How do you prevent mixed pick gauges from migrating between compartments?
Seat full-height paperboard or rigid dividers flush against the tray floor with zero bottom gap under the lid.
Can one outer box work for multiple pick gauge assortments?
Yes, if the outer shell accommodates the thickest pouch stack and the visible insert or window clearly identifies each gauge.
cta: Send the assortment by gauge and count, a set of filled envelopes and the intended removal sequence for a tube quotation. Include quantity and destination. Minimum 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 product value per order, excluding freight, samples and other fees.
sections: Separate gauge from the pack count

Dunlop's standard range includes several gauges and variety packs. Ask for the approved assortment by part number, thickness, finish and count. Two picks with a similar outline can belong to different variants. Print a readable gauge identifier on each envelope where it remains visible in the carrier, and keep counts on the packer's bill of materials.
Calculate height from full envelopes

An empty envelope is almost flat. A stack filled with picks, adhesive closures and folded seams can be thicker on one side. Assemble the full set on a flat surface and measure at the tallest edge. Turn alternate seams only if the identifiers remain visible. Compare a short lift-out carrier with a simple pull band using the heaviest configuration.
Try a missing-gauge exercise at the packing bench

Remove one envelope from a dummy assortment and ask a second person to identify the gap using the proposed loading sequence. A coloured tube label can describe the set without proving the contents. Provide an independent count or slot identifier if variants can be interchanged. Test the return action too: a player should be able to replace one envelope without emptying the tube.

Request separate prices for the presentation box, insert, sample and shipping outer.

title: Where to Support a Spring Capo Without Squeezing Its Handles
seoTitle: Where to Support a Spring Capo Without Squeezing Its Handles
summary: Kyser describes its acoustic Quick-Change model as spring-loaded. Let the buyer grip the frame on removal.
intro: Place a capo on a sheet of paper and trace its outline. The drawing tells you where the part sits, but a tightly cut pocket can press the handles just as a player would. Ask the capo supplier for the approved resting position and the frame areas the pack can support before cutting the first insert.
faq: Where should a packaging insert hold a spring-loaded guitar capo?
Support the rigid frame spine and leave clearance around the spring handles so the mechanism is not held under constant compression.
How do you make a spring capo easy to remove from a tight tray?
Cut finger-lift notches on opposite sides of the frame so the buyer grips the metal body rather than the rubber fret pad.
What should be checked before approving the lid height?
Place the instruction card or warranty leaflet inside the closed sample to confirm it does not press against the capo handles.
cta: Send a side view of the resting capo, the card thickness and a marked drawing of the permitted support points for an insert review. Include quantity and destination. Minimum 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 product value per order, excluding freight, samples and other fees.
sections: Mark the moving parts before drawing the nest

Kyser describes its acoustic Quick-Change model as spring-loaded. Different capo mechanisms require different packouts. For the buyer's exact part, mark the pivot, gripping pads and the handles' travel on two views. With the sample in its agreed resting position, select stable frame contact points and keep the tray walls clear of the moving handle.
Let the buyer grip the frame on removal

Compare a shallow frame saddle with a deeper pocket in the same board footprint. The deep version can control sideways movement yet encourage a person to squeeze the handles to extract the item. Cut a finger recess beside a supported section and observe someone opening the unlabelled sample. If their first instinct is to lever on the padded jaw, move the recess and repeat.
Close the lid with the instruction card installed

A thick instruction fold can bridge a recess and push down on the handle. Close the loaded box under its own normal closure and inspect the position of the card after reopening. Record the allowed paper stock, fold count and card position with the insert drawing. If several capo models share the same artwork, repeat the closure test for the tallest handle.

title: Sizing Three Glass Slide Pockets When the Outside Diameters Vary
seoTitle: Sizing Three Glass Slide Pockets When the Outside Diameters Vary
summary: Specify guitar slide box dividers using measured inner diameter, outer diameter and length, with finger access to lift the centre slide first.
intro: A player's ring size tells them whether a slide fits a finger. It tells a packaging buyer very little about how three slides will sit in a drawer. Ask for the outside profiles, lengths and packed weights, then trial the smallest and largest samples in the same finished divider before approving a common tool.
faq: How should pockets be sized for a three-piece glass guitar slide set?
Measure the maximum outside diameter including any flared lip on each slide, rather than relying on nominal inner ring size.
Which insert material protects glass slides best in a drawer box?
High-density die-cut EVA foam cushions glass edges well and prevents glass-to-glass contact better than thin single-ply paperboard.
Why test lifting the centre slide first?
If the middle slide sits flush with no finger relief, buyers cannot grip it cleanly while the outer two slides are still in place.
cta: Send the smallest and largest slide profiles, set weights and drawer opening direction for a divided-tray quotation. Include quantity and destination. Minimum 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 product value per order, excluding freight, samples and other fees.
sections: Trace the flare as well as the straight section

Dunlop gives separate inside diameter, outside diameter and length for its medium flared slide and notes variation in handmade pieces. For your range, measure several representative units at both ends and around the widest part. A channel based only on the centre diameter may pinch a flared rim while leaving the middle unsupported.
Try withdrawing the centre slide first

Set three dummies side by side in separate channels. Leave a pickup recess beside each body so a player can take the centre slide without nudging the neighbouring glass. Then check the thinnest slide for rolling or movement towards the end stop. If one large pocket fits the whole range poorly, compare replaceable end blocks with dedicated trays and quote the changeover work.
Check the drawer in its direction of travel

Pull the loaded drawer to its intended stop and inspect the end clearance and divider position. A face that separates glass at rest may bend enough to bring two pieces together during handling. Use witness material on dummies to locate possible contact, then agree the complete outer carton and transit assessment with the buyer. A clean bench check alone cannot establish parcel protection.

Mark the approved contact areas and the surfaces that must remain clear on a drawing of the packed accessory or its supplied case. Identify who supplies protective covers, who loads the retail set and who signs off the loaded sample. Compare the glass guitar slide trio drawer box concept with the outer carton specified for your distribution route. Request separate prices for the presentation box, insert, sample and shipping outer.

title: A Harmonica Gift Box That Lets the Player Keep the Original Case
seoTitle: A Harmonica Gift Box That Lets the Player Keep the Original Case
summary: Hohner lists a plastic snapcase with its Special 20. Compare one recess with a two-part presentation.
intro: A retailer wants the instrument visible when the lid opens. The musician wants the carry case after the presentation box goes into storage. Before choosing the window or the lining, decide whether the packer will present an instrument inside its closed case or display both pieces separately. The same footprint rarely serves both arrangements well.
faq: Can a harmonica gift box hold the instrument inside its original plastic snapcase?
Yes, provided the insert pocket is measured across the widest hinge and latch protrusions and includes a finger notch or ribbon lift.
What should be tested when adding a ribbon pull to a harmonica insert?
Thread the ribbon under the actual loaded snapcase and test repeated lifting to confirm the ribbon does not snag on the latch or tear the board slot.
What minimum order quantity applies to custom harmonica gift boxes?
MTT Packaging supplies custom rigid gift boxes from 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 minimum product value per order.
cta: Send the closed case dimensions across the hinge and latch, plus your preferred presentation layout, for a hinged-box quotation. Include quantity and destination. Minimum 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 product value per order, excluding freight, samples and other fees.
sections: Measure the closed case across the latch

Hohner lists a plastic snapcase with its Special 20. Ask the brand for its actual case revision and measure it closed, including the latch and hinge. Mark the lid-opening direction on the drawing. If the case must be removed to open it, place the pickup point where a thumb will lift the base without accidentally operating the latch.
Compare one recess with a two-part presentation

A single case pocket can keep the instrument in its supplied enclosure and reduce packing steps. A separate display pocket gives the retail team a clearer view, but adds a second handling operation and requires an approved contact area on the instrument. Price those operations separately. Ask the brand to approve handling of any surface that contacts the player's mouth.
Thread the ribbon through the loaded sample

Position the lift ribbon beneath the case body and try it with the full weight in place. A narrow ribbon running under one end can tilt the case into the hinge wall. Move it toward the centre of the load, then check whether a person can still find its free end with the instruction leaflet installed. Record that orientation in the packing photograph.
What to include in the supplier brief

Mark the approved contact areas and the surfaces that must remain clear on a drawing of the packed accessory or its supplied case. Identify who supplies protective covers, who loads the retail set and who signs off the loaded sample. Compare the cased harmonica hinged presentation box concept with the outer carton specified for your distribution route. Request separate prices for the presentation box, insert, sample and shipping outer.

Layout optionProsSample check

title: A Grey Target Mailer Has to Fit the Folded Rim
seoTitle: A Grey Target Mailer Has to Fit the Folded Rim
summary: Manfrotto describes a collapsible grey and white target that packs smaller than its open format. Keep closure flaps away from the working face.
intro: The open width tells a photographer how much target they can see. A packaging buyer needs a different measurement: the folded, sleeved target at rest, including the edge seam. I would start a mailer sample with that packed profile and agree how the customer can lift it without touching the working face.
faq: Why does a collapsible grey target need extra mailer depth?
Spring-steel pop-out targets relax slightly after folding, so measuring while hand-squeezed underestimates the resting thickness inside the carton.
How do you protect the calibrated grey surface from carton dust flaps?
Orient the mailer opening and inner dust flaps away from the working face, or keep the target inside its zip pouch during packout.
Should the target be packed inside its fabric pouch in the mailer?
Yes, if sold with a pouch, always size and approve the mailer with the target zipped inside that pouch.
cta: Send the model revision, packed dimensions, accessory list, quantity and destination for a folded photography grey target mailer review. Minimum 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 product value per order, excluding freight, samples and other fees.
sections: Measure the target after it has settled

Manfrotto describes a collapsible grey and white target that packs smaller than its open format. Obtain the maker's folding instructions for your target and measure a packed sample at several points around the rim. Record the highest overlap and the position of any pouch closure. Compressing the sample with a ruler will understate the depth the mailer needs.
Keep closure flaps away from the working face

Draw the closed mailer in section at the thickest point, including the sleeve seam and rolled corrugated side walls. Try placing the pull tab at the pouch edge. A tab beneath bare fabric may drag across the face on withdrawal. Compare a wider sleeve opening with a longer tab if the customer has to push the target out with a thumb.
Approve the arrival inspection with the target owner

Pack a representative target and its leaflet, then reopen the shipper in the intended sequence. Inspect for contact marks, creases and transferred ink using the owner's agreed criteria. Ask the owner to assess the opened target separately if optical acceptance is required. Record the selected shipping outer and distribution test before promising protection for a parcel route.
What to include in the supplier brief

Mark the approved contact areas and the surfaces that must remain clear on a drawing of the packed instrument. Identify who supplies protective covers, who packs the device and who signs off the loaded sample. Compare the folded photography grey target mailer concept with the device owner’s approved transport packaging. Request separate prices for the presentation box, insert, sample and shipping outer.

title: Sizing a Strap Tube Around the Buckle and the Webbing
seoTitle: Sizing a Strap Tube Around the Buckle and the Webbing
summary: Peak Design's Slide Lite illustrates a strap system with separate anchor connections. Keep metal hardware away from the visible textile.
intro: Roll a strap twice on the bench and you may get two different diameters. Add a buckle at the outside of one roll and it can catch on the tube wall. I would agree a repeatable packout with the strap supplier before approving a tube diameter or a foil wrap.
faq: How do you stop metal strap buckles from scuffing webbing inside a paper tube?
Fix a repeatable rolling method with a protective sleeve or folded paper collar separating metal adjusters from the main textile face.
Why set the strap adjuster to one position before sizing the tube?
Moving the buckle changes the coil diameter and where rigid hardware sits against the tube wall.
What should be tested with the finished inner liner?
Insert and withdraw the rolled strap and anchor pouch multiple times to verify smooth removal without snagging on the inner seam.
cta: Send the model revision, packed dimensions, accessory list, quantity and destination for a camera neck strap presentation tube review. Minimum 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 product value per order, excluding freight, samples and other fees.
sections: Set the adjustment before rolling

Peak Design's Slide Lite illustrates a strap system with separate anchor connections. List the components in your own kit, including spare anchors and any pouch. Agree the position of each adjuster and mark the starting end of the roll. Record the largest diameter after the roll has relaxed on the bench, with the actual keeper fitted.
Keep metal hardware away from the visible textile

Compare placing detachable hardware in a small pouch above the roll with wrapping it inside the centre. An upper pouch makes counting easier but adds height and may compress the webbing under the lid. Centre storage can hide a missing part. Test both arrangements with the widest webbing and the largest accessory bag intended for the same tube.
Check withdrawal with a finished liner

A plain board prototype can feel different from the finished inner wrap. Have another person close, open and withdraw the roll using the proposed paper band. Check for snagged stitching, a loose band or a buckle dragged along the tube wall. If the roll jams, revisit the winding method and liner seam before increasing every tube dimension.

Identify who supplies protective covers, who packs the device and who signs off the loaded sample. Compare the camera neck strap presentation tube concept with the device owner’s approved transport packaging. Request separate prices for the presentation box, insert, sample and shipping outer.

seoTitle: Packing a Camera L-Bracket Without Losing the Mounting Screw
summary: Really Right Stuff's installation guide shows how a plate interfaces with the tripod socket. Give the upright its own clearance.
intro: Lift a sample bracket from a shallow tray and watch what stays behind. A loose screw under the plate can mark the finish, and an envelope hidden beneath the insert can end up in the bin. Start with the fastener inventory and the exact bracket position in which the accessory supplier will deliver it.
faq: How do you pack a camera L-bracket without losing the mounting screw?
Place non-captive mounting screws and hex keys in a dedicated sealed pocket or snug press-fit foam slot separate from the main bracket cutout.
Why does an L-bracket need a stepped cavity?
The base plate and vertical side plate sit at 90 degrees, so a flat cutout leaves the upright unsupported or pressing into the lid.
What should be sent to MTT for an L-bracket box sample?
Send exact CAD or physical dimensions of the bracket, screw, and hex key, plus quantity from 1,000 pieces per design.
cta: Send the model revision, packed dimensions, accessory list, quantity and destination for a camera l bracket lift-off box review. Minimum 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 product value per order, excluding freight, samples and other fees.
sections: Identify captive and loose parts on the packing list

Really Right Stuff's installation guide shows how a plate interfaces with the tripod socket. For packaging, ask the buyer which screw is already installed, whether a tool is supplied, and whether the side plate can move. Measure the installed head at its highest projection. Draw an independent recess for that projection if the base otherwise rocks on it.
Give the upright its own clearance

A bracket standing on its narrow edge may overturn during loading. Lay the broad section in a stepped pocket and mark the unrestrained side arm in section. A taller inner shoulder can keep the lid skirt away from the metal edge but can make the bracket hard to lift. Give the operator a grip on the broad body and try unloading with the lid fully removed.
Count the hardware without tipping the tray

Fit a labelled envelope alongside the bracket with its opening clear of the extraction path. Ask a packer to distinguish a full kit from a deliberately incomplete dummy kit using the agreed count process. After handling the loaded sample, reopen it over clean paper and check the envelope closure and bracket finish before releasing the layout.

title: Three Filter Cases in One Drawer: Which Dimension Sets the Slot?
seoTitle: Three Filter Cases in One Drawer: Which Dimension Sets the Slot?
summary: Nikon lists screw-on filters by size. Decide which case the buyer can lift first.
intro: A buyer sends a list of three filter thread sizes. I can start a layout from that list, but I would price the divider after seeing the closed cases. A hinge, latch or raised label can set the slot width even when all three filters have the same nominal diameter.
faq: Should camera filter drawer slots be sized by filter thread diameter or case size?
Size each slot by the closed protective filter case outer dimensions, including any hinge or latch protrusion, because identical 77 mm filters can ship in cases of different thicknesses.
How do you prevent tall filter cases from catching a drawer sleeve?
Verify closed drawer headspace with the thickest case fully seated and allow finger clearance at the top edge so cases sit upright without tilting forward.
What insert materials work best for multi-filter drawer boxes?
High-density die-cut EVA foam or rigid paperboard partitions work well; EVA cushions heavier glass filter cases, while paperboard partitions reduce bulk.
cta: Send the model revision, packed dimensions, accessory list, quantity and destination for a camera filter trio drawer box review. Minimum 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 product value per order, excluding freight, samples and other fees.
sections: Measure each closed case at the thickest point

Nikon lists screw-on filters by size. Those designations help identify the filter but do not specify a supplier's retail case. Record the width across the latch, the thickness at the hinge, and the direction of the label. Trace a case standing on its intended edge. Use the largest measured envelope when evaluating a common slot.
Decide which case the buyer can lift first

Test removal of the middle case while the two outer cases remain loaded. A deep divider supports the cases yet can hide their labels or block a pinch grip. Try scalloping the divider near the label while retaining full support lower down. Compare the result with shorter dividers using the same three loaded cases.
Set a sign-off condition for mixed sets

If two versions share one carton, photograph both packouts with the drawer partly open. Ask a second person to identify each filter without opening its case. Then pull the drawer to its normal limit and check for case tilt and sleeve contact. Quote a keyed divider separately if a shared layout permits a part to be loaded in the wrong position.
What to include in the supplier brief

Mark the approved contact areas and the surfaces that must remain clear on a drawing of the packed instrument. Identify who supplies protective covers, who packs the device and who signs off the loaded sample. Compare the camera filter trio drawer box concept with the device owner’s approved transport packaging. Request separate prices for the presentation box, insert, sample and shipping outer.

title: Sizing a Lens Hood Insert Around the Bayonet Tabs
seoTitle: Sizing a Lens Hood Insert Around the Bayonet Tabs
summary: Nikon identifies the HB-90 as a bayonet hood for specific lenses. Try a saddle before specifying a full ring.
intro: On a packaging drawing a hood looks like a simple ring. Turn the sample over and the small mounting tabs become the first things to inspect. For a hood sold separately, I would establish where the buyer can hold the base and how the insert carries the body before quoting a circular cutout.
faq: Why is a saddle support often better than a full ring for a bayonet lens hood?
A saddle supports the main cylindrical barrel while leaving the delicate plastic bayonet locking tabs free from radial squeeze.
What must be checked on a hinged box for a petal-shaped lens hood?
Check the closing arc of the hinged lid against the tallest petal tip so the lid does not clip the hood rim as it closes.
How do packers keep asymmetric petal hoods oriented correctly?
Add an alignment notch or clear visual orientation guide in the packing instruction and sample record.
cta: Send the model revision, packed dimensions, accessory list, quantity and destination for a bayonet lens hood hinged box review. Minimum 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 product value per order, excluding freight, samples and other fees.
sections: Mark the mount on a side elevation

Nikon identifies the HB-90 as a bayonet hood for specific lenses. For your own model, mark its mounting features, tallest petal and permitted support band on two views. A single outside diameter hides the projection of a tab. Ask for the as-packed sleeve too, since its seam can change how the part settles.
Try a saddle before specifying a full ring

A continuous ring can present a tidy opening but leaves little room for fingers. Two saddles can expose the base for removal. Their spacing matters: rotate a dummy through every position the packer can load and check whether a tab can come to rest directly on either saddle. Key the insert only if orientation matters and operators can identify the index.
Inspect the hinge side after closure

Place plain witness tissue over a dummy at its highest point and cycle the lid with the literature installed. A crease flags possible contact for closer inspection. Compare relocating the literature with lowering the saddles, then confirm the revised sample still leaves enough base exposed for removal. Record the orientation on the packout sheet.
What to include in the supplier brief

A printed outline cannot distinguish two similar cables. Place the supplier label face up, or give the sleeve a window that exposes the existing identifier without altering the device packaging. Ask a second person to identify the variant with the recorder still seated. If they have to unpack it, change the label position before artwork approval.
Load both extremes and operate the drawer

The thickest folded harness can catch the sleeve mouth. The thinnest can move into the recorder cavity if a common divider stops short. Trial both configurations using their actual folded leads and inserts. Record loaded drawer travel and whether the identifier stays visible after normal handling. intro: Two sealed tins and a scoop need three separate decisions: how the tins are supported, where the scoop can be lifted, and how the filled assembly closes and travels. Measure the finished tins with lids and labels and provide the scoop in its intended protective wrapper. sections: Start with the finished tin, not nominal tea weight

A tin described as holding 50 g of tea does not establish its actual diameter or height. Measure the widest closed tin, lid projection and any seam or label, and record its filled weight. Include the range if two suppliers or tin sizes will be used. Note which decorated surfaces cannot tolerate rubbing. Agree whether both tins can use one cavity size; a common cavity may simplify assembly but still needs a fit check for the smallest tin.
Decide how each tin is supported and removed

A snug circular opening can position the tin for presentation while leaving insufficient space for a finger. Consider a finger recess, a suitable lift tab or a removable tray, then test with the heaviest and lightest filled tin. Support should be assessed around the body and beneath the base rather than relying on the lid or a fragile label. Record where the buyer should grip and whether the second tin stays seated during removal.
Give the scoop its own wrapped position

Measure the complete scoop including any sleeve, tie or guard. A shallow channel can make the tool visible; a covered pocket may suit a loose or flexible accessory but adds a separate removal step. Check that the scoop cannot press against the box cover or tin, and agree who supplies and inserts it. The illustration is a design concept: it does not establish a food-contact approval or a completed manufacturing project.
Separate presentation from food contact and shipping

This presentation box assumes the tea remains in separately sealed primary packaging. If the scoop or an inner material touches tea directly, request the relevant material declaration for the actual use and destination market; do not infer suitability from a generic food-safe label. The US FDA explanation of food-contact substances describes why the material and intended use matter. Distribution risk is another decision: specify the outer shipper and evaluate the complete packed set for its route. ISTA advises reassessing tests when product, packaging or process changes may affect performance.

Send closed-tin drawings, filled weights, photos of lids and labels, the wrapped scoop, quantity by artwork, target market, packing location and delivery route. Ask for the box, insert and optional bag or card as separate line items, with sampling and freight shown separately. sections: Measure the filled and sealed pack

A flat dieline misses the thickness created by the coffee and filter inside. Collect representative filled sachets across the product range, including the widest seal and any tear notch. Measure the height, overall width and thickness in the intended orientation. Record how many sachets go in each compartment, since a stack behaves differently from one packet. Balance presentation and removal

A separate paperboard divider can hold flavors in order, but dividers consume internal width and can lean or catch flexible seals. Check the narrowest and widest sealed packets in each compartment. A finger recess or open top may help access, but must not expose fragile seals to lid pressure. Agree the selection order and check that removing one sachet does not displace the rest. Place the information card outside the crush path

Measure the card or folded leaflet as supplied, including any envelope. A dedicated end slot keeps it visible, but it should not push the adjacent sachet or prevent the drawer closing. Test the drawer when it is loaded

The empty tray may slide well while the filled set catches at the sleeve entrance or bows at the base. Load the specified number and heaviest sachet combination, check the opening force by hand, and look for snagged seals, bowed dividers and contact between tray contents and sleeve. Repeat with actual samples and the intended outer shipping pack; agree acceptance criteria for displacement and damage rather than claiming a universal clearance.
